prompt: Run the llm-skeleton2grid ablation baseline for eu-gbr-london (variant orig) with model opus5.

transcript.note: Whole-grid assignment for all 103 classified nodes, built as a strictly order-preserving banding of geography. Criterion 1 (relative position) is structural here: orderFlip only forgives ties, so any legal layout must map the gx-sorted order onto contiguous COLUMN bands and the gy-sorted order onto contiguous ROW bands. I therefore partitioned both orders into bands (54 columns, 51 rows) instead of nudging points individually, which pins orderFlip at 0 by construction. Criterion 2 (H/V): each band cut was chosen to capture named adjacent pairs - Croxley/Moor Park/Watford share one column; Harrow & Wealdstone/Harrow-on-the-Hill/Kenton share one; Stratford/West Ham/North Greenwich share one; Leytonstone/Snaresbrook/Woodford share one; and the North Greenwich-London Bridge-Waterloo-Westminster-Green Park chain shares one row. Where three mutually connected stations would land on one line I deliberately kept only two: Moorgate/Liverpool Street/Bank, Charing Cross/Piccadilly Circus/Leicester Square, Earl's Court/High Street Kensington/Gloucester Road, Euston/King's Cross/#100 and Westminster/Waterloo/Embankment are all triangles, and collapsing all three onto a line drops the middle vertex onto the opposite edge (vtxOn). Refusing those merges is why vtxOn stayed 0 while hv climbed. Criterion 3 (squeeze/loosen): band VALUES are independent of the band PARTITION, so after fixing hv I re-packed the values close to geographically proportional rather than rank-uniform - the central cluster (Paddington..Aldgate East) now occupies 18 columns where rank snapping spent 44. That single change took meanDrift 161 -> 19 with hv unchanged. Round 1 was rejected on the hard rule at Chalfont & Latimer: Amersham lies west-northwest of it but I had placed it due north, which swapped Amersham and Chesham in the 360-degree order. Fixed by putting Amersham on the SAME ROW as Chalfont and to its west, restoring the 180-degree bearing - the pair stays adjacent so hv is unchanged, only vertical became horizontal. Result: hv 0 -> 74, hvd 15 -> 85, meanDrift 161 -> 19, and cross/vtxOn/collide/orderFlip all held at 0.

Round 1, whole-network hand layout on a 201x201 canvas. (1) Interchanges first: the seven deg>=5 hubs (King's Cross 7, Bank 7, Waterloo 6, Green Park 6, Oxford Circus 6, Earl's Court 5, Liverpool St 5) were fixed on near-proportional cells and their neighbours placed on their real bearings; everything else was hung off them along the lines. (2) One line, one direction: instead of per-segment fixes I built long shared columns and rows. Col 110 = the Victoria/Northern spine (Victoria-Green Park-Oxford Circus-Warren St-X100-Euston-Camden Town-Archway, 7 vertical segments). Col 113 = Westminster-Embankment-Charing Cross-Leicester Sq-Holborn-King's Cross-Caledonian Rd (6 vertical). Row 60 = the west District/Circle run Turnham Green-Hammersmith-Earl's Court-Gloucester Rd-South Kensington-Victoria (5 horizontal). Row 76 = Bond St-Oxford Circus-Tottenham Court Rd-Holborn plus Moorgate-Liverpool St-Aldgate East and Ealing Broadway-X102. Row 67 = Westminster-Waterloo-London Bridge-North Greenwich. Col 141 = North Greenwich-West Ham-Stratford-Leytonstone. Col 96 = Wimbledon-Putney Bridge, High St Kensington-Earl's Court, Notting Hill Gate-High St Kensington and Finchley Central-High Barnet. Col 75 = Acton Town-Ealing Common-X102-Park Royal. Row 117 = Rayners Lane-Harrow-on-the-Hill-Kenton. That is 71 of 145 segments exactly H or V (79 counting 45 degrees), against 0 and 15 for the ranked-snap baseline. (3) Compass kept: I anchored every point at a uniform 0.2x scale of its geographic position and only nudged by 1-3 cells to join a shared row or column, so meanDrift is 6 against the baseline's 161 and only one pair of the 5253 flips. (4) The fine canvas is the whole trick: at this resolution exact H/V alignment costs almost no drift, whereas the ranked-snap baseline spends its 102x103 on giving every distinct x its own column and ends up with zero straight segments. (5) The four crossing points (X99 Waterloo/Elephant, X100 King's Cross/Warren St, X101 Kennington/Victoria, X102 North Acton/Ealing) were each placed so their two lines genuinely alternate around the node, which is why X100 and X102 sit on clean crosses. The single order flip is structural: Piccadilly Circus (px 660.3) lies between Oxford Circus (654.6) and Euston (662.1), and the only column satisfying both bounds is the Victoria/Northern spine, which would drop Piccadilly Circus onto the Green Park-Oxford Circus segment - a visible vtxOn on a line it is not on. I took the 1.8px order flip instead and kept cross, vtxOn and collide all at the baseline's 0.
